> The existing Tags property should probably be marked as obsolete and return all convert all objects to string.

Just to comment on that, we are not going to obsolete it in this release as it will be a big breaking for libraries using the old way of activity (e.g. asp.net, http client,...etc.). Also, we'll not change the Tags behavior and we'll return only the items which has string values. that is for less confusion and also for the sake of the performance.

review_comments: `aSource.StartActivity("a2", default, null)` - could we test with this as well? This should trigger `GetRequestedDataUsingParentId`, which would in turn would call `GetRequestedDataUsingContext`, with auto-generated traceid. (from an earlier PR which added this behavior)

passing null parent Id will not trigger GetRequestedDataUsingParentId at all because the parent Id is null and will just call GetRequestedDataUsingContext with default context. Is this the scenario you want test?
I added this test too.
Could you make it explicit that this traceid will be used by the Activity, should we chose to create it?
should we leave a comment in the ActivityContext summary that this is inspired from OT? W3C spec has nothing like `IsRemote`, so it may hint users where/what is the motivation for having IsRemote
sure. I'll add the comment
@tarekgh Hey I just noticed working on some code in OTel that you can't specify events in the StartActivity call. You can specify pretty much everything else. Should we add events too?
Also there is no AddLink method. Links you have to specify at creation?

> I just noticed working on some code in OTel that you can't specify events in the StartActivity call. You can specify pretty much everything else. Should we add events too?

StartActivity arguments mainly the things needed for sampling decision to decide if want to create the activity or just avoid that and sample it out. If you look at the OT sampling specs, you'll find events are not needed there https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/master/specification/trace/sdk.md#sampling. But anyway, you can add events after creating the activity. 

> Also there is no AddLink method. Links you have to specify at creation?

This was proposed before and then got removed because there was a claim that shouldn't allow adding links after creating and starting the activity. OT specs saying `During the Span creation user MUST have the ability to record links to other Spans. Linked Spans can be from the same or a different trace.`. so, the spec is explicit mentioning the links should be provided during the Span creation. But anyway, later if we find any scenario need to add links after starting the activity, we can consider it.

CC @cijothomas @reyang
What Tarek said is my understanding as well.

That all makes sense. What I'm doing right now is working on a unit test. It needs the Activity created very specifically. So it's not a normal use case. I think I can make it work with reflection. The links are a bit of a challenge. I'll mention you guys on the change once I have it working so you can see what I'm up against, and then we can decide if any changes are warranted.
Not `ActivityTagDictionary`? 🤷‍♂️
No, because the collection has to keep the list in order. in general Dictionaries don't promise that.

This looks like it could fail to set the new key when InterlockedCompareExchange loses the race. We should be able to set the new key regardless.

AddTag() appears to have the same issue and I suppose I missed it in the past.
nevermind, I misread the code, there is no issue here.
is null value also treated as string, and is returned along with `Tags`?
Yes, in old AddTag(string, string) allowed null.
Thanks for the writing.
done. thanks.
As the behavior is more that of a `Set` method than a `Add` method, shouldn't we call this as Set?

No, Add behavior is different than Set behavior. Add will always add a new entry even if there is previous entry with the same key is added. Also add can allow null value. This is the whole point we adding 2 APIs and not just one.
